slides.label: What an eval measures
slides.source_text: In practice Separate the case, the grader and the trial Test case Export a net-100 invoice with 21% VAT. Grader Parse the CSV and check that net, VAT and gross are 100, 21 and 121. Trial One fresh attempt with a recorded model, prompt, tools and environment. Evaluate the resulting artifact. A message saying “done” is not the outcome.

slides.label: Acceptance cases
slides.source_text: In practice Make the expected behavior explicit Case Expected result Net 100.00; VAT 21% VAT 21.00; gross 121.00 Net 100.00; VAT 0% VAT 0.00; gross 100.00 Net 0.05; VAT 10%; half-up cents VAT 0.01; gross 0.06 Customer name: ACME, Ltd One customer field after CSV parsing For this exercise, round VAT half up to cents, then add it to net. The business rule must come from the task.

slides.label: Grading methods
slides.source_text: In practice Use the strongest practical check for each claim Deterministic check Parse CSV, assert values and run regression tests. Written rubric Assess explanation quality and completeness against named criteria. Human calibration Check ambiguous cases and compare model-judge scores with human decisions. A different judge model does not remove bias. Blind labels and vary answer order where practical.

slides.label: Repeated trials
slides.source_text: In practice One success answers a different question Illustrative outcomes for one case: fail fail pass fail fail At least one success in five attempts: yes All five attempts successful: no Observed single-attempt success rate: 1 / 5 This small sample does not establish production reliability. Report task coverage, repeats and uncertainty.

slides.label: Trace evidence
slides.source_text: In practice Record the observable run Inputs, configuration, tool requests, results and timestamps. Final files or external state, check output and exit statuses. Usage categories, retries, failures and any unavailable evidence. Telemetry is not a full transcript, and neither guarantees access to hidden model reasoning.

slides.label: Annotated trace
slides.source_text: In practice A repeated step is a question to investigate Observed step What to ask Read calc.py; edit it; read it again Did the second read inspect the changed code? Repeat a failed tool call Did the environment or arguments change? Restate the plan after a handoff Did this restore missing requirements? Label a step waste only after checking its purpose and effect.

slides.source_text: In practice Keep failed runs in the comparison Per trial Record Identity Case, variant, run number and versioned environment. Outcome Acceptance checks, rubric scores and evidence paths. Work Uncached input, cache writes/reads, output and retries. Operational result Time, total cost, review effort and error reason. Aggregate success rate and total spend over all trials. Do not report only successful attempts.

slides.label: Grading exercise
slides.source_text: In practice Score two synthetic outputs 10 minutes — no model call needed A: net=100, VAT=21, gross=121 for BOTH 21% and 0% orders. B: correct totals for both; customer ACME, Ltd is unquoted. Grade against the four cases. Which outputs fail? What evidence is still missing? Output: a scored worksheet with explanations. Neither candidate is ready to accept.

slides.label: Token volume and cost
slides.source_text: Count the work Count each billing category separately Category What to record Uncached input New input processed at its applicable input rate. Cache writes and reads Separate token counts and the configured cache rates. Generated output Output usage, including billable reasoning where applicable. Bill = sum of each category’s tokens × its rate, plus any separate tool or service fees.

slides.label: Worked cost example
slides.source_text: Worked arithmetic One cache-hit request: about five cents Illustrative usage and rates Cost 19,000 cached input × $0.20 / million $0.0038 3,700 new input × $4 / million $0.0148 1,600 output × $20 / million $0.0320 22,700 input + 1,600 output in total $0.0506 Assumed rates, not a measured bill. Without the cache hit: $0.0908 input + $0.0320 output = $0.1228.

slides.label: Choose the route
slides.source_text: In practice Start with how the work will run Need Check before choosing Daily interactive work Native client, plan limits and actual monthly usage. Custom service, batch or CI Supported API authentication, rate limits and a budget. Organizational controls Identity, data handling, audit, residency and procurement requirements. Compare current offers against these requirements. Detailed shopping questions are in reference material.

slides.label: Useful context
slides.source_text: Context quality Keep the facts that the next decision needs Keep The invoice rule, failing case, relevant code, decisions and latest test result. Summarize or remove Duplicate file dumps, stale logs and abandoned approaches, once their useful findings are captured. Watch for missed requirements and repeated work. There is no universal “dumb zone” or safe fill percentage.

Use the instruction-file convention your harness actually loads. Keep standing rules short and specific.

slides.label: Compare instruction variants
slides.source_text: In practice Exercise · compare two versions fairly 10 minutes A: the long instruction file. B: the shorter version. Use identical task inputs, repo state, model and tools. Record: acceptance results, all usage, time and retries. Repeat runs if available; inspect failures before choosing. Output: a comparison worksheet and one justified decision. A smaller prompt that drops the VAT rule loses.

slides.label: Continue or reset
slides.source_text: In practice Choose from the state of the task Unrelated next task Start fresh with its own scope and needed project context. Same task, long history Summarize the goal, evidence, decisions, failed attempts and next check. Check what survives compaction. Neither a fresh session nor a summary has zero context cost.

slides.label: Subagents
slides.source_text: Split the work · subagents Delegate a question; ask for evidence back Fresh helpers need a self-contained task and relevant inputs. Forks can inherit existing history. Keep intermediate investigation in the helper’s context; return findings with file references. Review the result. Delegation adds coordination cost and does not itself isolate filesystem access. Example return: VAT calculation locations, the failing path, supporting lines and unresolved questions.

slides.label: Coordination and containment
slides.source_text: In practice Two separate design decisions Orchestration Who gets a task, what it depends on and who integrates the result. Isolation What files, credentials, processes and network endpoints the tools can access. A dashboard or Git worktree does not by itself enforce a security boundary.

slides.label: Ticket lifecycle
slides.source_text: In practice One ticket, explicit state transitions Ready: invoice rule + scope + acceptance cases Claimed: one owner + lease + retry budget Working: permitted workspace + progress evidence Review: patch + checks + unresolved gaps Accepted: reviewer confirms the requested behavior Failed or blocked work returns with evidence. A green tool run does not automatically publish a change.

slides.label: Static ticket walkthrough
slides.source_text: In practice Walk the invoice ticket without a live service Event Expected state or action Worker finds missing VAT rule Blocked; request the rule before changing behavior. Two workers claim the same ticket One claim wins; the other does not start editing. Tests pass but escaping is untested Review records the gap and adds an acceptance check. Exercise: explain who owns each decision and what evidence is attached.

slides.label: Tool boundary
slides.source_text: In practice Specify the environment the worker receives Allow the repository paths and commands required by the ticket. Scope credentials and network access to the necessary services. Use separate edit workspaces; enforce time, attempt and spend limits outside the prompt. Review mounts, egress and permissions in the actual runtime.

slides.label: Loop failure controls
slides.source_text: Define done Match each failure to a control Failure Concrete control Repeats the same failed repair Limit attempts; require a new hypothesis before retrying. Weakens tests to make them pass Review the test diff; run independent acceptance checks. Changes unrelated behavior Scope allowed paths; inspect the complete diff. Prompts help communicate these rules. Enforce the important boundaries in tools, permissions and review.

slides.label: Review capacity
slides.source_text: In practice Limit work in progress to what can be reviewed Before starting Assign the reviewer and agree on the return format. While work runs Stop filling the queue when review capacity is exhausted. At acceptance Inspect the integrated result, including interactions between patches. More workers can move the queue downstream. Measure completed, accepted work.

slides.label: MCP and CLI
slides.source_text: In practice Compare the complete interaction MCP Tools exposed through a client/server protocol, with structured inputs and supported authentication paths. CLI Commands executed by a shell tool, with help, arguments, output and error handling. Both can reach local or remote services. Both need appropriate credentials, permissions and review.

slides.label: Tool overhead
slides.source_text: In practice Definitions are only one part of the cost MCP schemas may be loaded eagerly or discovered on demand, depending on the client. CLI use also consumes shell definitions, help text, command output and repair attempts. Compare successful completion, tool failures, total usage and latency. Measure the actual client configuration. There is no universal cheaper interface.

slides.label: Local model memory
slides.source_text: In practice Active parameters are not the RAM requirement Stored weights depend on total parameters, representation and quantization. Inference also needs a KV cache, activations, runtime buffers and overhead. Offloading can move weights to CPU memory or disk, trading memory for transfer time. Approximate weight storage: parameters × bits per weight ÷ 8. This is a lower-bound estimate, not a fit guarantee.

slides.label: Static hardware exercise
slides.source_text: In practice Estimate storage, then list what is missing 10 minutes — illustrative hardware scenario 35B total parameters; 3B active per token; four-bit weights. Weight-only storage ≈ 35B × 4 / 8 = 17.5 GB. Would a machine with 16 GB available memory fit it? What could offloading change? What must you measure? Output: a qualified feasibility note. Include KV cache, buffers, quantization overhead and speed.

slides.label: Local or hosted
slides.source_text: In practice Choose from constraints and observed results Local may fit You can meet the quality, latency and memory requirements in an approved local environment. Hosted may fit Its capability and operations meet your requirements, and the data path and commercial terms are acceptable. Inspect the whole workflow: local inference does not stop tools or telemetry from using the network.
